full_text_en:
Xia Yonglin v. Haitong Securities Co., Ltd., Wuxi Business Department — Dispute over Confirmation of Stock Subscription Rights

Plaintiff: Xia Yonglin, male, born on January 9, 1952, a resident of Wuxi City, Jiangsu Province.

Defendant: Haitong Securities Co., Ltd., Wuxi Business Department.

Legal Representative: Xiao Jianwei, General Manager of the Business Department.

Agents ad litem: Cai Xiaoming and Zhang Zhong, lawyers of Liangxi Law Firm, Wuxi, Jiangsu Province.

Plaintiff Xia Yonglin filed a lawsuit with the Chong'an District People's Court of Wuxi, Jiangsu Province, against Defendant Haitong Securities Co., Ltd., Wuxi Business Department (hereinafter referred to as Wuxi Business Department) concerning a dispute over confirmation of stock subscription rights.

The plaintiff alleged: The securities company's allotment delivery slip is an unalterable contract. The defendant denied that the plaintiff had won the lottery, refused to deliver the shares in accordance with the allotment slip issued to the plaintiff, thereby depriving the plaintiff of his stock subscription rights and causing losses to the plaintiff. The plaintiff requests the court to confirm that he has the right to subscribe to 1,000 shares of Wuliangye new shares, and order the defendant to compensate the plaintiff for mental damages in the amount of 5% of the subscription funds, i.e., RMB 10,339.

The defendant argued: The plaintiff's actual starting allotment number for subscribing to the new shares was 000001499909, and this number and the subsequent 13 numbers were not winning numbers. The allotment delivery slip mentioned by the plaintiff serves only as a notice and is not a legal document evidencing a transaction with the client. Although the defendant erroneously conveyed the allotment number due to a work error, there is no causal relationship with the plaintiff's failure to win the lottery, nor did it cause any loss to the plaintiff. The plaintiff's claims lack factual and legal basis and should be dismissed.

The Chong'an District People's Court of Wuxi, Jiangsu Province, found the following facts upon trial:

The defendant, Wuxi Business Department, is an agent of the securities exchange. On March 13, 1997, the plaintiff Xia Yonglin entrusted Wuxi Business Department to handle stock trading procedures on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange (SZSE). In March 1998, the SZSE conducted an online offering of Wuliangye new shares at an issue price of RMB 14.77 per share. On March 27, 1998, Xia Yonglin paid RMB 206,780 to Wuxi Business Department to subscribe for 14,000 shares of Wuliangye new shares. On March 31, 1998, the main computer system of the SZSE trading system automatically assigned a sequential issuance allotment number for every 1,000 valid shares subscribed, and then transmitted the issuance allotment number records to each securities trading outlet. On the same day, after receiving the records, Wuxi Business Department issued to Xia Yonglin an allotment delivery voucher. The voucher indicated that the starting number for Xia Yonglin's 14 issuance allotment numbers was 00141131. On April 2, 1998, *China Securities Journal* published the results of the lottery drawing for the Wuliangye stock issuance allotment numbers, where all issuance allotment numbers ending with 136 constituted a group of winning numbers, and each winning number entitled the holder to subscribe for 1,000 shares. After checking, Xia Yonglin confirmed that one of his issuance allotment numbers had won the lottery, but on that day, 1,000 shares of Wuliangye stock were not delivered to his account, and the RMB 206,780 subscription funds he had paid were fully returned to his account. Xia Yonglin repeatedly negotiated with Wuxi Business Department but failed to achieve his objective, and therefore filed this lawsuit.

It was further found that on March 23, 1998, the SZSE issued a notice to all outlets regarding the modification of the allotment number fields for online issuance of stocks and funds. The notice stated that effective from the issuance date of "Fund Kaiyuan," the SZSE would change the previous practice of storing allotment number content in the "Transaction Time" (FCJSJ) field of transaction records, and instead would place the issuance allotment number and winning number content in the last 12 digits of the "Counterparty Sequence Number" (FDFXH) field in the return data records, and requested that all outlets modify the relevant programs by the 24th of that month. After receiving this notice, the defendant Wuxi Business Department failed to modify the relevant programs in a timely manner, causing the computer system's allotment number reading program to continue reading and printing the data content 00141131 from the "Transaction Number" (FCJHM) field as the issuance allotment number. However, in the database file of the plaintiff Xia Yonglin's transaction records, the content of the "Counterparty Sequence Number" field was 000001499909. After discovering the error, Wuxi Business Department reposted the issuance allotment numbers in the lobby on April 1, 1998. According to the inquiry results from the SZSE's voice mail inquiry service system, the issuance allotment number 000001499909 for subscribing to Wuliangye shares, and the subsequent 13 allotment numbers, were all not winning numbers.

The above facts are confirmed by evidence including the notice copy of the delivery voucher, the Wuliangye stock issuance announcement, the SZSE notice on modifying the allotment number field, the database file of Xia Yonglin's subscription transaction records, the investor's certificate, and the faxed inquiry results from the SZSE voice mail system.

The Chong'an District People's Court held: The relationship between the plaintiff Xia Yonglin and the defendant Wuxi Business Department is one of agency. Wuxi Business Department failed to modify the allotment number reading program in a timely manner as required by the SZSE notice, resulting in the conveyance of an erroneous allotment number during the process of acting as agent for Xia Yonglin's subscription of Wuliangye new shares. Wuxi Business Department was at fault. Article 66, Paragraph 2 of the *General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China* provides: "If an agent fails to perform his duties and thereby causes damage to the principal, he shall bear civil liability." Wuxi Business Department, due to its own fault, caused Xia Yonglin to incur certain economic losses from traveling back and forth to negotiate regarding the allotment number issue, and therefore shall bear liability for compensation, with the specific amount to be determined discretionarily by the court. Wuxi Business Department does not have the authority to control the issuance allotment numbers for online offerings of new shares. The delivery voucher it issued to Xia Yonglin did not reflect the true intention of the SZSE, which holds the authority over the issuance allotment numbers for online offerings of new shares, and therefore cannot serve as valid evidence for confirming the issuance allotment number. Moreover, there is no causal relationship between Wuxi Business Department's work error and whether Xia Yonglin's issuance allotment number would win the lottery. Accordingly, Xia Yonglin's claim to confirm his right to subscribe to 1,000 shares of Wuliangye new shares is not supported. Although the erroneous conveyance of the issuance allotment number by Wuxi Business Department caused some mental displeasure to Xia Yonglin, it did not rise to the level of causing him to suffer significant physical or mental pain or trauma. Xia Yonglin's request to order Wuxi Business Department to compensate for mental damages at 5% of the subscription funds clearly constitutes an abuse of rights and lacks factual and legal basis, and this court does not support it. Accordingly, the Chong'an District People's Court of Wuxi, Jiangsu Province, hereby adjudicates as follows:

1. The claim of Xia Yonglin to confirm the right to subscribe to 1,000 shares of Wuliangye new shares is dismissed.
2. Wuxi Business Department shall compensate Xia Yonglin for economic losses in the amount of RMB 2,000.

The litigation costs of RMB 1,015 shall be borne equally by both parties.

After the first-instance judgment was pronounced, neither party appealed.
